title: Relativity leaves only the symmetric potentials integrable: a classification of homogeneous polynomial potentials for the additive relativistic Hamiltonian
shortTitle: Relativity leaves only the symmetric potentials integrable
oneLine: For H = √(1+p²) + V with V a homogeneous polynomial of degree at least three, only one-coordinate and radial potentials keep a second first integral.
abstract: A particle in the plane under a potential V, with relativistic kinetic energy, has the Hamiltonian H = √(1 + p₁² + p₂²) + V(q₁, q₂). Przybylska, Szumiński and Maciejewski (2023) found that relativity destroys almost all of the integrable cases known for the classical Hamiltonian ½|p|² + V, and suggested that for homogeneous polynomial potentials only the one-coordinate and radial potentials survive; they settled degrees three to five by another route and conjectured that generic potentials are non-integrable. This candidate proves the suggestion for every degree k ≥ 3: a nonzero real homogeneous polynomial potential admits a second first integral, meromorphic on the natural complex phase space of H and independent of H, if and only if, after a rotation, V = c q₁^k or (k even) V = c (q₁² + q₂²)^{k/2}, that is, if and only if V is invariant under a translation or under all rotations. The result is new for k ≥ 6, and a local version needs integrability only near two explicit complex phase curves. Complex-coefficient potentials that have a nonisotropic linear factor and whose isotropic factors q₁ ± iq₂ do not have multiplicity exactly k/2 are integrable only when they are a power of one nonisotropic linear form; in particular every generic homogeneous polynomial potential is non-integrable, which proves the stated consequence of the 2023 conjecture (its arithmetic part remains open). The new ingredient is a rigidity theorem at a vanishing transverse eigenvalue: a first nonconstant transverse term produces two independent periods on a hyperelliptic phase curve, which make a finite jet of the normal holonomy non-commutative, and the Morales–Ramis–Simó theory forbids this. Limits: integrability is complex-meromorphic, so smooth integrals on a restricted real region or one energy level are not excluded; degrees one and two, non-homogeneous potentials and three or more degrees of freedom are outside the statements; isotropic monomials and the exact-half multiplicity case remain open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Theorem A (proof, main): for V real, nonzero, homogeneous of degree k ≥ 3, H = √(1+|p|²) + V is meromorphically integrable on its complex phase space if and only if it is rationally integrable, if and only if after a real rotation V = c q₁^k or (k even) V = c (q₁² + q₂²)^{k/2}; the second integrals are p₂ and the angular momentum. New for k ≥ 6; for k = 3, 4, 5 the 2023 paper reached the real conclusion by another route.
Theorem 6.1 (proof): a real potential not of these forms is already non-integrable near one of two explicit complex phase curves attached to a direction where |V| is maximal on the unit circle.

Proposition 3.1 and Theorems 4.1, 5.1 (proof): at a nonisotropic proper Darboux direction the transverse eigenvalue satisfies λ = (n+1)(kn+1) for an integer n, so λ ∈ {0, 1} ∪ [2k−1, ∞); λ = 0 forces V = a x^k (zero-eigenvalue rigidity, no classical counterpart in positive degree) and λ = 1 forces an even-degree radial power.

Theorem B and Corollary C (proof): a complex potential with a nonisotropic linear factor and isotropic multiplicities different from k/2 is integrable only if it is a power of one nonisotropic linear form; with no isotropic factor, generic potentials are non-integrable, the stated consequence of the 2023 conjecture.
Open: isotropic monomials (q₁ + iq₂)^α (q₁ − iq₂)^β with α ≠ β, α, β ≥ 1, and potentials with an isotropic factor of multiplicity exactly k/2.

narration:
Imagine a particle gliding across a flat table, pushed around by a force field. Its motion is called integrable when something besides the energy is also conserved. Integrable motion is regular and predictable; without that second conserved quantity, the motion can turn chaotic.

For force fields given by simple polynomials, classical mechanics knows many integrable cases. But what happens when the kinetic energy follows Einstein's relativity instead of Newton's formula?

Przybylska, Szumiński and Maciejewski showed that relativity is destructive for almost every classical integrable case. They suggested that only two kinds of potential survive: those that depend on a single coordinate, and those that are perfectly round. They settled the smallest degrees, three to five, by comparing with the classical lists, and left the general question open.

This release proves their suggestion for every polynomial degree from three upwards, so the result is new beyond those smallest degrees. A real potential of this kind is integrable exactly when, after turning the axes, it is a power of one coordinate, or a power of the distance from the centre. Only potentials with a continuous symmetry survive, and the extra conserved quantity is the matching momentum.

The proof looks along the direction in which the potential is strongest. There, straight-line motions exist, and the small wobbles across them are governed by a single number, which can only take its two simplest values at that direction. In either case, following nearby orbits once around a loop produces two independent periods, and an integrable system cannot allow that unless the potential has the symmetry.

The same reasoning settles most potentials with complex coefficients, and shows that a generic polynomial potential is never integrable in the relativistic model.

Some limits matter. The conserved quantities considered are those that extend to the complex version of the motion, so smooth quantities on a restricted region are not ruled out, and two complex families remain open.

This is an unrefereed candidate, checked by internal AI-assisted review, proof audits and symbolic computation rather than by outside peer review, and its proofs, programs and limits are open for anyone to inspect.

relatedWorks.citation: Combot (2013), Meromorphically integrable homogeneous potentials with multiple Darboux points. Preprint, arXiv:1301.6621. Period determinant from commuting monodromy (Section 4.3) and Theorem 1, an alternative route to the eigenvalue-one case.

Combot (2016), Integrable planar homogeneous potentials of degree −1 with small eigenvalues. Annales de l'Institut Fourier. The closest classical precedent: extremal direction (Lemma 3.1) and rigidity at small eigenvalues (Theorem B, Lemma 4.5).

Duval and Maciejewski (2015), Integrability of potentials of degree k ≠ ±2. Second order variational equations between Kolchin solvability and Abelianity. Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems. Higher variational equations at special eigenvalues.

Kimura (1969; issue dated 1970), On Riemann's equations which are solvable by quadratures. Funkcialaj Ekvacioj 12(3), 269–281 (JaLC DOI 10.24546/0100498821; Kobe University Repository record). The classification used in the spectral restriction (Appendix A).

Maciejewski and Przybylska (2005), Darboux points and integrability of Hamiltonian systems with homogeneous polynomial potential. Journal of Mathematical Physics. The Darboux-point relation for generic potentials, its version with isotropic factors (Theorem 2.3) and the multiplicity counts used for Theorem B.

Morales-Ruiz (registered as MoralesRuiz), Ramis and Simó (2007), Integrability of Hamiltonian systems and differential Galois groups of higher variational equations. Annales Scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure. Corollary 2(ii), which turns the holonomy computation into an obstruction.

Przybylska, Szumiński and Maciejewski (2023), Destructive relativity. Chaos. The question, the strong necessary condition (Theorem 3), the classification for degrees three to five (Section V) and the conjecture on generic potentials (Section VI).

Szumiński, Przybylska and Maciejewski (2024), Chaos and integrability of relativistic homogeneous potentials in curved space. Nonlinear Dynamics. A different relativistic Hamiltonian, cited for context and not used.

Szumiński and Przybylska (2025), Integrability and chaos of relativistic Hamiltonian systems in 2D Riemannian manifolds. Nonlinear Dynamics. The special-energy hypergeometric reductions (Section 3.1, eqs. (31)–(34), Theorem 3) used in flat form.
